key_insight: GUIDED replaces topology-tied demand initialization with a network-agnostic virtual-link embedding, enabling GNNs to transfer more reliably across different urban graphs.
engineering_relevance: This makes traffic assignment surrogates more deployable for transportation planning by improving out-of-network generalization while also cutting training cost.
method: Encode travel demand as a scalar on auxiliary virtual links instead of fixed node features.
Use a modular initialization layer, GUIDED, before a HetGAT surrogate.
Enable inductive transfer learning across networks without artificial input homogenization.
evidence_signal: Across multiple urban topologies, the HetGAT+GUIDED model matched state-of-the-art single-network accuracy, improved robustness under shifted demand and low-data settings, and reduced training time per epoch by about 50%.
watch_item: The approach still depends on how well the virtual-link representation and heterogeneous graph design align with the target transport domain, so transfer gains may vary for very different network structures.
paper_title: GUIDED Network-Agnostic Feature Initialization for Spatial Transferability in GNN-based Models
